explanation: States that for n ≥ 3, floor(n / (4·tan(π/n))) = floor(n²/(4π) − π/12). This is the hedged OEIS comment "Usually (perhaps always?)", and the area formula for a regular unit-side n-gon is correct. The restriction n ≥ 3 avoids the degenerate n = 2 (offset 2, a(2) = 0) and is harmless. Because the exact area equals n²/(4π) − π/12 − O(1/n²), the claim can fail only when n²/(4π) − π/12 lies just above an integer, so `research open` is a fair tag. The formalization is faithful.
